notes: Each case targets a decision the skill exists to get right, not a command it can run. Cases 2 and 3 are the ones a model gets wrong even with an earlier version of this skill: asked to lint a pull request it reaches for `mekiki diff`, whose "no change" says nothing about the state of the touched skills. The others cover linting an inherited corpus and starting to fix, treating warnings as work, and inventing a guard name.

evals.prompt: We inherited ~180 skills from another team. Audit them and tell me what to fix.
evals.expected_output: Runs mekiki lint, notices the missing-baseline note, and settles the baseline with the user before proposing any repair — explaining that without one no rule can reach error severity, so a newly added skill is never held to the higher bar. Does not begin editing skills.
assertions: explains that a baseline makes new skills stricter than pre-existing ones
does not start editing skill files in this turn

evals.prompt: This PR touches two skills in acme-toolkit. Check it before I send it for review.
evals.expected_output: Runs `mekiki lint <path> --changed` so the report covers the skills this PR touched, rather than linting the whole tree. Explains that the corpus is still evaluated in full and only the report is narrowed, and that the exit code follows the narrowed report so the inherited backlog cannot fail the review. Mentions `mekiki diff` only as the separate answer to whether the corpus regressed.
assertions: uses mekiki lint --changed, not a full lint of the tree
does not present the pre-existing backlog as this PR's work
does not reach for mekiki diff as the answer to "check this PR"

evals.prompt: mekiki でこの PR を lint して
evals.expected_output: Chooses `mekiki lint <path> --changed`, not two snapshots and `mekiki diff`. Says which revision it is comparing against (`origin/HEAD` unless told otherwise) and reads the notes first: a report with no findings because no skill was touched is stated as such rather than reported as a clean corpus. If it also runs `diff`, it labels that as a different question — whether the corpus regressed — and does not let a `no change` result stand as the answer to whether the touched skills are sound.
assertions: selects lint --changed for a request phrased as linting a PR
names the base revision it compared against
does not report "no change" from mekiki diff as the state of the touched skills

evals.prompt: Fix everything mekiki reported. Here it is: one L8 error about spend wording with no guard declared, and eleven L6 warnings.
evals.expected_output: Asks which guard skill the org uses for that risk tier rather than inventing a name, and explains that a declaration naming a skill that does not exist protects nothing. Treats the eleven warnings as triage rather than a to-do list, and for any it does repair, moves the deterministic work into scripts/ with a test instead of deleting the sentence that tripped the rule.
assertions: does not invent a guard skill name
does not treat warnings as required work
repairs L6 by relocating logic to scripts/, not by deleting prose
